payload.rationale: To resolve to Yes, the 2026 annual average must exceed 1.28 C. The first 8 months of 2026 average 1.224 C. To reach an annual average above 1.28 C, the final 4 months (September-December) must average greater than 1.39 C. August 2026 reached 1.40 C, and NOAA reports a greater than 90% chance of a very strong El Nino during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter of 2026-27. This strong El Nino provides a plausible mechanism for sustained, extreme temperature anomalies late in the year. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that maintaining an average above 1.39 C for four consecutive months is an exceptionally high hurdle, and global temperatures can be volatile. The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is that the rapidly strengthening El Nino could push late-year anomalies significantly higher than 1.40 C, easily pulling the annual average above the threshold.
limitations: The annual target remains unknown, with four months missing.
